the use of lactobacillus strains as starters in the fermentation of Spanish-style green olives is feasible and that the inoculum must be adapted to the alkaline environment.
inoculation of green olives with a starter culture of L. pentosus at high pH, above 9, is possible and that the inoculum must take into account the initial survival.
the utilization of starter cultures of L. pentosus Cect 5138 at alkaline pH is feasible and that this strategy can be applied in the industrial manufacture of Spanish green olives.

the development of a starter culture for the Spanish-style green olive fermentations.
the development of a new technology for Spanish-style green olives, based on the application of starter cultures of L. pentosus at the time of brining.

a new approach to the utilization of starter cultures in the Spanish-style green olive processing, which is based on the inoculation of the brine at alkaline pH with lactobacilli, thus avoiding the use of acidulants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the utilization of starter cultures of lactic acid bacteria for Spanish-style green olives fermentation at alkaline pH is a feasible alternative to the traditional practice of spontaneous fermentation.
the inoculation at high pH of green olives with L. pentosus CTC 5138, a strain isolated from a traditional Spanish green olive fermentation, is feasible and effective.

the use of starter cultures of L. pentosus CEC5138 in the green table olive fermentation process is feasible, and can improve the process, but it should be used at the beginning of fermentation, and with an inoculum of about 10(6) CFU/g of olive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the utilization of starter cultures for the Spanish-style green olive fermentations is possible, but it is necessary to take into account the low tolerance of the starter cultures to the alkaline environment and to use a high enough inoculum to compensate the initial viability loss.
the use of L. pentosus starter culture in the Spanish-style green olive processing is a viable alternative, which could be of great interest to the olive industry.
inoculation of lye-treated Spanish-style green olives with Lactobacilli starter cultures can be a good strategy to accelerate and improve the fermentation process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of starter cultures of L. pentosus is a feasible strategy to accelerate Spanish-style green olive fermentations.

the utilization of starter cultures of L. pentosus CEC 5138 at pH 9 is feasible and that this bacterium is a good candidate to develop starter cultures to be applied at high pH in the Spanish-style green olive industry.

the use of starter cultures of L. pentosus at alkaline pH is a promising alternative to improve Spanish-style green olive fermentations, as it reduces the time of fermentation and the population of Enterococcaceae and Enterobacteriaceaea, which are potential spoilage bacteria.
